title: Maximum Side Length of Square Within Threshold
description: Given an `m x n` integer matrix `mat` containing non-negative integers and an integer `threshold`, return the **maximum side length** of a contiguous square subgrid (`k x k`) whose sum of elements is less than or equal to `threshold`, or `0` if no such square exists.
hints: Build a 2D prefix sum table so the sum of any k x k square ending at (r, c) can be computed in O(1) time.
Because all entries are non-negative, while scanning cells (r, c) you only ever need to test side length (best + 1): if it fits and has sum <= threshold, increment best by 1 for an O(m * n) solution.

examples.explanation: The 2x2 square of all 1s has sum 4 <= 4, while every 3x3 square has sum > 4, so the answer is 2.
Every single cell is 2 > threshold 1, so no valid square exists and the answer is 0.
The entire 2x2 matrix sums to 10 <= 10, giving side length 2.
